record.original_question: Instead of lifting by polynomials in Thurston’s algorithm for interval maps, consider the family p(x) = -|x|^alpha + c with alpha > 1, equivalently after affine rescaling the family x maps to k - k|2x - 1|^alpha from the unit interval to itself with 0 < k <= 1. Given an initial map f0 with preperiodic or periodic kneading sequence, does Thurston’s algorithm converge for this specific nonpolynomial lifting family?

evidence.quote: For instance computer experiments suggest that we can choose the pk’s from a family of the form p(x) = −|x|α + c where α > 1 . (To be more precise, we must first change coordinates with an affine map so that the boundary 0,1 maps to 0. This yields the family of maps x 7→ k − k|2x − 1|α from the unit interval to itself where 0 < k ≤ 1.)

Question 2. Given f0 with a preperiodic or periodic kneading sequence does Thurston’s algorithm converge for the specific family above. There is a proof only for α an even integer, which is the polynomial case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real parameter $\alpha>1$ and a parameter $k\in(0,1]$, consider the one-parameter family of unimodal interval maps
$$ p_{k,\alpha}:[0,1]\to[0,1],\qquad p_{k,\alpha}(x)=k-k\,|2x-1|^{\alpha}, $$
each of which has a unique critical point at $x=1/2$ and sends the boundary $\{0,1\}$ to $0$. (When $\alpha$ is an even integer, $p_{k,\alpha}$ is, after an affine change of coordinates, the real polynomial $x\mapsto -|x|^{\alpha}+c$.)

To any unimodal map $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with critical point $c=1/2$ one associates its kneading sequence, the itinerary of the critical value under $f$ with respect to the partition $[0,c)$, $\{c\}$, $(c,1]$. Call $f$ admissible if its kneading sequence is either eventually periodic (preperiodic) or periodic.

Thurston's pull-back algorithm in this setting is defined as follows. Given an initial admissible unimodal map $f_0$ with kneading sequence $K$, recursively choose, for each $n\ge 0$, the parameter $k_{n+1}\in(0,1]$ so that $p_{k_{n+1},\alpha}$ realises the same combinatorial pull-back data as $f_n$ on its (pre)periodic critical orbit, and set $f_{n+1}=p_{k_{n+1},\alpha}$ (equivalently, lift $f_n$ through the family $\{p_{k,\alpha}\}_{k\in(0,1]}$ via the prescribed kneading data $K$).

Question: For every $\alpha>1$ and every initial admissible unimodal map $f_0$ whose kneading sequence is preperiodic or periodic, does the sequence $(f_n)_{n\ge 0}$ produced by this Thurston-type algorithm converge to a map in the family $\{p_{k,\alpha}:k\in(0,1]\}$ with kneading sequence equal to that of $f_0$?

It is known that convergence holds when $\alpha$ is an even integer (the polynomial case). The problem asks whether convergence persists for all real $\alpha>1$.
artifact.category_tag: Thurston pull-back algorithm for interval maps
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located work on Thurston's algorithm for real polynomials and on a "tower algorithm" generalizing Thurston's scheme to unimodal interval maps (Tiozzo and others), which establishes convergence for unimodal maps of high entropy and exhibits non-convergence at low entropy in related settings. No source was found that specifically resolves convergence of the Thurston-type lifting algorithm for the non-polynomial family $x\mapsto k-k|2x-1|^{\alpha}$ for general real $\alpha>1$. Status appears unresolved beyond the polynomial (even-integer) case.

status_evidence.title: Metrics on trees I. The tower algorithm for interval maps (Tiozzo)
status_evidence.snippet: A scheme that unifies Thurston's iterative scheme... converges for unimodal maps of high entropy, with examples where it does not converge for unimodal maps of low entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations of Thurston's algorithm to unimodal interval maps have been studied, with mixed convergence results, but the specific family $k-k|2x-1|^{\alpha}$ for general $\alpha>1$ is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: The W. Thurston Algorithm Applied to Real Polynomial Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Effective procedure for constructing critically finite real polynomial maps using the Thurston algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: Recent treatments of Thurston's algorithm for interval maps remain focused on the polynomial case.
